value.rationale: Fixed-wave-number density relaxation is a distinct, physically motivated observable not controlled by bulk spatial Gaussian scaling alone. The exact critical spatial frequency and t^-2 observation-time window identify how Fourier modes change from nonoscillatory to damped oscillations; the sharp t^-3/2 branch-edge term supplies an absolute error and separates continuous-spectrum relaxation from isolated modes. The result is self-contained and quantitatively predictive without requiring a separate paper-sized generalization.
